name: June Lukuyu
bio:
June is an Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Washington, where she leads the Interdisciplinary Energy Analytics for Society (IDEAS) Research Lab. Originally from Kenya, she draws on her lived experiences to study energy challenges and develop solutions for Africa and other underserved regions and communities. Her research is grounded in an understanding of the needs, ambitions, and distinct challenges and opportunities of the communities she works with.

Her work connects research, policy, and community engagement through her roles as a Fellow at the Energy for Growth Hub and African Tech Futures Lab, a Research Fellow at the Kigali Collaborative Research Centre (KCRC), a principal investigator with the e-GUIDE Initiative, and member faculty at the UW Clean Energy Institute (CEI). She also serves as the current Board President of Spark Northwest.

June holds a Ph.D. from the University of Massachusetts, an MSc. in Renewable Energy Systems from Loughborough University, and a BS in Engineering Science from Smith College.

name: Eliane Nirere
bio: Eliane earned her master's degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering with a specialization in Energy Systems from Carnegie Mellon University Africa. Her research focuses on the planning and implementation of technologies that enhance sustainable energy access in underserved communities.

name: Ahana Mukherjee
bio: Ahana has a bachelor's degree in Civil & Environmental Engineering from UCLA and a master's degree in Energy, Civil Infrastructure, and Climate from UC Berkeley. She has experience designing and implementing utility-scale battery energy storage systems and commercial solar and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Her research interests include renewable energy power systems, electrification, energy access, and socially-conscious equitable designs.

name: Kwame Donkor
bio:
Kwame earned his bachelor’s degree in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from KNUST in Ghana, specializing in power systems. He has extensive experience designing and installing commercial- and industrial-scale electrical and automation systems, leading technical teams, and managing projects focused on renewable energy and off-grid electrification.

Kwame is passionate about using data analytics, geospatial analysis, and machine learning to advance reliable, sustainable, and inclusive energy systems. Through an interdisciplinary lens, he explores how insights from grid-edge sensors, weather observations, and other sources can support the equitable delivery of reliable electricity, particularly in resource-constrained regions. His research interests include power-grid resilience to climate shocks, machine-learning applications in power systems, and the economic feasibility of grid-hardening and modernization strategies.

Outside of his research, Kwame enjoys working out, running, hiking, exploring the outdoors, and spending time with friends.

name: Miquilina Anagbah
bio: Miquilina's passion for clean energy access and mini-grid development is electrifying! With a strong foundation in power systems analysis, design, and operations, Miquilina aims to revolutionize how we think about electrification for sustainable development. She earned her Master's in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Carnegie Mellon University Africa. Her research dives deep into mini-grid techno-economic analyses and grid integration studies and looks for new ways to push the boundaries of what's possible. Outside the lab, she loves studying new languages and playing the piano.

name: Aya Alayli
bio: Aya has a strong passion for grid planning, sustainable development, policy, and energy equity. She earned her Bachelor's from the Electrical and Computer Engineering department here at UW and has previous experience working within different aspects of the electric power industry. Her research interests center around community-led energy transitions, energy justice, and resiliency. Outside of the lab, Aya enjoys exploring Seattle, reading, and spending time outdoors
